title: Define the boundary and joint governance with foundational DPI exchange
requirements:
- Define a capability boundary; countries map what foundational DPI already provides
- Require purpose limitation, minimum necessary access and legal authority
- Describe a cross-sector forum, requirements process, service agreements and escalation
- Extend foundational-DPI integration planning beyond national identity to trust services, civil registration, geospatial references and payments
- Allow shared DPI-H services, not only endpoints, to provide health-specific functions
- Separate health identity from legal-identity enforcement; allow pseudonymous tokens and care without verified ID
- Present the foundational exchange example as one illustrative pattern
- Limit terminology API access to authorised use cases
